cuts.reason: Cuts from the wide title-card shot ('When the World Ends', crowd fleeing a tsunami) into the couple's calm two-shot on the promenade, instantly setting up the contrast between world-ending chaos and their deadpan indifference.
Hard cut from the punchline line 'You really don't know us at all' straight to the black branded end card, snapping off the joke right after the payoff for a quick outro/CTA.

reaction_shots.description: Single continuous shot holding on the couple's deadpan, unbothered banter and expressions as a giant tsunami looms behind them; the shot never cuts away, letting their non-reaction to the apocalypse (and the 'thought this was the kissing part' misdirection) carry the entire comedic beat instead of advancing any plot action.

pacing_notes: Editing is front- and back-loaded with quick cuts bracketing one long held shot: a 1.3s title-card cut establishes apocalyptic stakes fast, then the video holds on a single unbroken ~11.5s two-shot for the whole dialogue exchange, letting the deadpan delivery and comic timing breathe without any interior cuts, before snapping to a 0.8s black end card for branding. The lack of mid-scene cutting during the joke keeps focus on performance/dialogue rather than visual rhythm, then the pacing accelerates again sharply for the outro.
